title: Impact of Gravity on Changing Magnetic Field Orientations in a Sample of Massive Protostellar Clusters Observed with ALMA
question: How do magnetic field orientations at 0.01 pc core scale and 10^3 au envelope scale relate in massive protostellar clumps, and what role does gravity play in changing them?

data.arrays: ALMA main array, C43-1 and C43-4
data.sensitivity: 1 sigma rms 30 to 70 uJy in Stokes Q and U

what.value: Gas temperatures (~100 K, >300 K locally) from CH3OH in NGC 6334, used as dust temperature

evidence.quote: The dust temperature is approximated by the gas temperature reported in (cite: liu_J2023a)
a dust emissivity spectral index $\beta$ of 1.5 (cite: beuther2007b)

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image continuum Stokes I, Q, U
recipe.method: Calibration by ARC, phase self-cal on Stokes I, tclean of line-free continuum
theta = 0.5 arctan(U/Q), 3 sigma cutoff on Q and U, rotate by 90 deg
Compare PA from C43-1 and C43-4 (>250 m), absolute differences folded to 0-90 deg; sources convolved to common linear resolution; G28 and I18360 excluded; K-S test vs random 3D angles
key_parameters: Sampling at 0.5 of the C43-4-restricted beam

recipe.goal: Column density map and projected Rayleigh statistic vs density
recipe.method: 1.3 mm continuum to N_H with kappa=1 cm2/g at 230 GHz, beta=1.5, T from CH3OH; normalized PRS (alignment measure) vs column density; RO with local gravity
assumptions: beta=1.5; dust opacity 1 cm2/g at 230 GHz; dust temperature = gas temperature (~100 K)

answer_key.quantity: K-S probability, entire sample RO vs random

evidence.quote: We find a probability of $6 \times 10^{-6}$ that the two are drawn from the same population.
We find a probability of $2 \times 10^{-9}$ that the two are drawn from the same population.

answer_key.quantity: K-S probability for NGC 6334 I, In, IV, V

evidence.quote: 0.07, 0.002, $6 \times 10^{-5}$, and 0.4 for NGC 6334 I, In, IV and V, respectively
We found a probability of 0.6 that the two are drawn from the same population.
